gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the Fluance RT81+ cartridge sits on a pre-aligned headshell screwed onto the tonearm that, according to Digital Trends, 'will accommodate a range of higher-end carts', so you can upgrade the whole cartridge and not just the stylus.
standout_why: I compared against stylusandsound.com and platterandplinth.com (both opened 2026-11-13). stylusandsound.com says the RT81+ has a 'Headshell with Audio Technica VM95E Cartridge' but never says the headshell takes other cartridges. platterandplinth.com covers only the original RT81 (AT95E) and says nothing about whether its headshell takes other cartridges. Both rivals already have the other main compatibility facts: the AT-LP70X takes any VM95-series stylus, Sony 'states other styluses are not supported' on the PS-LX3BT, and the AT-LP120XUSB needs a dedicated stylus for 78s. platterandplinth.com also claims the Sony has aptX Adaptive. The fewbetter.com URL ChatGPT got now shows an unrelated page with no turntable content. The finding that would have stood out more, Sony's own FAQ listing the PS-LX3BT codecs as SBC and aptX only (no AAC, no LDAC, no AVRCP volume control), I saw only in search snippets because every Sony page returned 403 or was blocked. So it cannot be used.
decides: It confirms the pick and doesn't change it. Among the decks ChatGPT showed, the RT81+ has the widest upgrade path: you can swap the stylus or the whole cartridge on its headshell. The AT-LP70X/LP70XBT is limited to VM95-series styli on a fixed VM95C cartridge, according to the rivals. The Sony PS-LX3BT can't be upgraded at all, because Sony only supports its own stylus and the factory cartridge, according to platterandplinth.com, which cites Sony. A shopper who expects to upgrade should lean to the RT81+ over the LP70X.
